title: Carbon-price index | Europe
question: How do carbon prices in Europe differ across climate and CE settings?
caption: Carbon-price indices for Europe, comprising ENE, ENW, EUE, EUM, EUW, in all ten climate/CE scenarios from results_allCE_261008.csv. Each curve is the weighted mean of exact Price|Carbon [USD_2010/t CO2e] source prices. Weights use baseline_noce reported industrial GHG emissions in 2019, normalized within this group and held fixed across every scenario and year. Colours identify the five CE settings using the shared report palette; solid lines denote NDC (ndc_*) and dashed lines NDC+LTT (baseline_*). Squares denote no CE, open circles EU-only CE and filled diamonds EU-plus-partners CE. EU+ covers 17 participating model regions, rather than worldwide adoption. Prices are in constant 2010 USD per tonne CO2-equivalent. Source-year coordinates and signs are preserved; straight segments connect the supplied observations. Missing prices with positive weights yield gaps; zero-weight prices do not invalidate an index. Coincident curves are not displaced. Each region has its own linear price scale, including zero. Weights and raw regional contributions are exported alongside the figure data.
